chapter: Records, rivals and New Orleans bands
title: Records with Francois Mosley's band and Mac and Mac in Chicago
summary: Punch lists the personnel on the Francois Mosley record and the pianist on the Mac and Mac session.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh, I wanted to ask you about Frankie Halfpaint Jackson. You made a record with him, huh? Oh, yeah. I made a record with him. You remember who was in that band?

Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. Charlie Ducasse, myself, Fred Reed on piano. And Charlie Ducasse on guitar and that boy, Lil Sax on tenor. Fred Howard on alto. He played alto on clarinet. And what else? Fred on piano, me on trumpet. Al Wynn on trombone. Al Wynn. I got a letter from him the other day. Little Sax's name is what? Robert Crowder. Everybody called him. You know who he was, Kenta? Y'all didn't know Cecil. He used to play with Earl Hein.
Well, I don't know. Cecil was Little Sax's mother's brother. That was his uncle, see. And he showed him a whole lot.
He was ranger in music for all of Chicago, Little Sax. He's a good ranger.
Who was the piano player with Mac and Mac? You remember that record you made with Mac and Mac?
Yeah, James Hemingway. That was his name, James Hemingway. And he made the record, huh? Yeah, he made the record.
